plan.rationale: Six evaluated points, all numerically passed, compiled, and saturating 32768 smem with 3 blocks/SM and identical 16.78 MB simulated DRAM. Latencies: 128x64x64/s1/sw0=234.82; 64x128x64/s1/sw16=235.12; 64x128x32/s2/sw16=221.79; 64x128x64/s1/sw8=214.47; 64x128x32/s2/sw8=203.69; 64x128x32/s2/sw4=203.69 (tied best). Swizzle values 4 and 8 gave identical latency and no DRAM change, confirming the analytic panel-reuse feature still is not materializing in simulator traffic; swizzle is kept open only as a probe and traffic weight stays low at 0.5. block_N=[128] and block_M=[64,128] retained (128-M row still unsampled). block_K=[32,64] and stages=[2,3] concentrate on deeper-pipeline variants; s1 points are dominated. Pipeline weight stays 2 to keep pushing toward num_stages=3 with block_K=64, which remains untested. Launches 0.75 favors larger/fewer tiles; footprint 1 is non-differentiating since all points hit the cap. Hard 32768 cap retained for portability. Metal checks execute exact source/config/TIR; CUDA binary is not executed, and GB10 latencies are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements. This is exploratory and not a claim of global optimality; the next hypothesis is that num_stages=3 (possibly with block_K=64 or the unsampled block_M=128 row) yields lower simulated latency than the current 203.69 us best.
